clue.text: Stephenson worked in it, recruiting gang in Gateshead centre

indicators.note: recruiting means taking someone in, so one piece is enlisted inside the other

parts.note: the Sage Gateshead is the music centre on the Tyne quayside
a gang is a team of workers

explanation.surface: A railway pioneer hires a work gang at a Tyneside venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gateshead centre' looks like a request for the middle letters of Gateshead, but it is the concert venue, the Sage, which takes in TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stephenson, builder of the Rocket locomotive, was a leading engineer of the era of steam railways.

clue.text: In Paris you put in laps: they make your muscles stronger

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a cat laps milk, that is sips it
tu is the familiar French word for you

explanation.surface: Swimmers in Paris do lengths to build up their muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laps' reads as swimming lengths, but it is the verb for drinking, SIPS, which has TU put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are abdominal exercises done to strengthen the stomach muscles.

clue.text: Waugh's diarist

definitions.meaning: the novelist Waugh's first name, as in the author of Brideshead Revisited
John ... was a seventeenth-century English diarist

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one person, Waugh's diarist, but it is two separate people sharing the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn Waugh was the novelist; John Evelyn kept a famous diary of Restoration England.

clue.text: Trounced, using same cards but in different order

indicators.note: putting the letters in a different order is a plain instruction to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Someone loses badly at cards despite using the same deck shuffled differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To be massacred in a game is to be trounced, beaten heavily.

clue.text: 19's idea wouldn't go wrong with brief preparation

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters go astray into a new order

parts.note: prep is a short form of preparation, as in school homework

explanation.surface: A plotter is sure a scheme cannot fail even with little planning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' is the anagram signal: the letters of WOULDNT GO plus PREP make the answer; 19 is FAWKES.
explanation.definitionFit: The plot to blow up Parliament in 1605 was the scheme Guy Fawkes was caught carrying out.

clue.text: Pay a quick visit to collect Latin material

indicators.note: to collect means to gather something inside

parts.note: to pop in is to make a brief call

explanation.surface: Someone drops by briefly to pick up some Latin homework.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplin is a plain-woven cotton fabric, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Home Counties menagerie had up for leaks

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
a menagerie is a collection of animals, a zoo

explanation.surface: A zoo near London is prosecuted over leaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had up' sounds like being taken to court, but it turns SE ZOO upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To ooze is to leak slowly, as liquid seeping out.

clue.text: Slate degrees in metal-working

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
working suggests the letters being worked into a new shape

parts.note: BAs are Bachelor of Arts degrees

explanation.surface: Graduates criticised for their metalwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal-working' reads as a craft, but 'working' is the anagram signal on the metal, and 'degrees' are plural Bachelor of Arts awards.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate someone is to criticise harshly, the same as lambasting them.

clue.text: Nitric oxide and nitrogen satisfied a student of such elements

parts.note: NO is the chemical formula of nitric oxide
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
to have met a need is to have satisfied it
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A chemistry student is pleased by two gases.
explanation.walkthrough: Nitric oxide and nitrogen are themselves non-metallic, so the clue words describe the elements the answer classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, the answer describes elements that are not metals, such as nitrogen and oxygen.

clue.text: He abandoned the cause for 19's offence

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so these letters drop out

parts.note: the letters he as written
a cause is a reason

explanation.surface: A man deserted the cause he stood for.
explanation.walkthrough: HE abandoning THE leaves T; 19 is FAWKES.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotting to blow up the King and Parliament was high treason, the crime Fawkes was executed for.

clue.text: Armstrong and Miller, say, take a quick nap with setter in Jordan's arms

indicators.note: in places the run of letters inside the outer pair
the arms of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: zz is the comic-strip sign of a snooze
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Two comedians nap alongside the setter, cradled by a model.
explanation.walkthrough: Armstrong and Miller suggest the comedy duo, but Louis Armstrong and Glenn Miller were jazz musicians. Jordan's arms are J and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Armstrong and Glenn Miller were both celebrated jazz musicians, so they serve as examples.

clue.text: 19's primary target (also the sixth)

parts.note: the king Fawkes aimed to kill was the first of his name in England and the sixth in Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is the clever bit: the same king reigned in Scotland as the sixth of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1605 plotters intended to kill the reigning monarch, who was king of England and of Scotland under different numbers.

clue.text: Classes make them up in geography lab

indicators.note: the letters that make them up sit inside the given words

explanation.surface: Classes concoct things in the geography lab.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a phylum is a major taxonomic group, ranking above a class.

clue.text: One includes merry game round Sunday school, singing from the same hymn sheet

definitions.text: singing from the same hymn sheet

indicators.note: includes means one piece holds the rest inside

parts.note: the letters one as written

indicators.note: round means one piece goes about another
merry suggests tipsy, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: S for Sunday and S for school

explanation.surface: A party game at Sunday school ends with everyone singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merry' reads as describing the game, but it is the anagram signal; 'round' and 'includes' are two nested containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being singing from the same hymn sheet is an idiom for agreeing with the official line.

clue.text: Plant does business with worker in spy network

parts.note: to trade is to do business

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
a worker is an ant, as in a worker ant

explanation.surface: A firm deals with an agent planted in an intelligence ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradescantia, the spiderwort, is a common garden and house plant.

clue.text: Strange tale on a CD's untrustworthy as evidence

indicators.note: strange signals letters in an unusual order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An odd story recorded on a disc cannot be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal evidence rests on individual stories rather than systematic data, so it is unreliable.

clue.text: Analysed figures but not, I see, old politicians

indicators.note: not means the named letters are left out

parts.note: statistics are figures that have been analysed
I see gives I and C, the letter sounding like see

explanation.surface: A pollster rejects old politicians' numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Statists believed in strong central state control; the word is an old term for politicians.

clue.text: Leaves about ten, dancing in groups

indicators.note: about means one piece is placed around another

parts.note: to leave is to quit

indicators.note: dancing means the letters move about

explanation.surface: Someone leaves around ten while groups dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A quintet is a group of five performers, so the plural means such groups.

clue.text: Theatrical device used in "King Lear"? Not quite the padding for his childlike outpourings!

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is missing

parts.note: an undersheet is bed padding to protect against a wet bed

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare prop doubles as protection for an old king's babyish tears.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear in his dotage behaves like a child, and the outpourings hint at bedwetting, which an undersheet guards against.
explanation.definitionFit: A thunder sheet is a hung metal sheet shaken to make storm noise, as in Lear's heath scene.

clue.text: 19 was one mixed-up type in history

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: history is the past
pi or pie is printers' type jumbled together

explanation.surface: Fawkes was a muddled character in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type' reads as a sort of person, but it is printing type.
explanation.definitionFit: Papist is a hostile term for a Roman Catholic, as Fawkes was.

clue.text: His function was violently to secure king's unfortunate end

definitions.text: His function was violently to secure king's unfortunate end

parts.note: f is the mathematical symbol for a function

indicators.note: to secure here means to hold something firmly inside
violently suggests the letters being thrown about

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: His job was to bring about the monarch's violent death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violently' rearranges WAS to AWS, which secures K and E; the whole clue describes the plotter's aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Fawkes guarded the gunpowder meant to kill King James.

clue.text: Sign on staff when one left ill after eating odd portions of rice

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside
ill suggests something gone wrong, so the letters rearrange
odd portions are the first, third letters and so on

explanation.surface: Someone feels sick after a rice meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' rearranges ONE LEFT into TENOLEF, which eats RC.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor clef is a musical symbol placed on a stave to fix pitch.

clue.text: Scoundrel has an Irish accent, not British

indicators.note: not means the named letter is left out

parts.note: a brogue is a strong Irish accent

explanation.surface: A villain speaks with an Irish lilt rather than an English one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest rascal, a scoundrel.

clue.text: Exciting events as Armada lost rear and scattered

indicators.note: scattered means the letters spread into a new order
lost rear means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: The Spanish fleet loses its back ships and disperses.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama means exciting events, as in plenty of drama.

clue.text: Extremely skilful crew's dexterity

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the outer letters

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew

explanation.surface: A highly skilled crew displays dexterity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' reads as very, but it takes S and L from skilful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is skill with the hands, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Second thoughts about repulsing man on board not good

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: repulsing means driving back, so the word is turned around
not means the named letter is left out

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece

explanation.surface: Someone has second thoughts about pushing back a board member.
explanation.walkthrough: KNIGHT without G is KNIHT; driven back it gives THINK.
explanation.definitionFit: A rethink is a second consideration, second thoughts.

clue.text: Coitus interruptus by regular guests in old county

indicators.note: interruptus means broken into, so letters go inside

parts.note: coitus is sex

indicators.note: regular means every second letter

explanation.surface: Lovemaking is interrupted by the guests in a southern county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interruptus' is lifted from the Latin phrase for withdrawal, here signalling insertion. Sussex is an English county, now split into East and West Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Sussex was a single county of south-east England before it was divided into East and West.

clue.text: They're allowed to enter rescheduled heats

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside
rescheduled means rearranged

parts.note: to be let is to be allowed

explanation.surface: Competitors are permitted to join rearranged heats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rescheduled' rearranges HEATS to ATHES; LET enters.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes are the competitors who run in heats, the 'they' of the clue.
